description:
src/methods/mod.rs:31,41,54,55,71,72,104,105 — every `state`, `old_state`, `new_state`, `query_state`, `old_query_state`, `new_query_state` field is typed `String`. jmap-types exports `State` (a transparent `#[non_exhaustive]` newtype over String, RFC 8620 §1.2), specifically intended for these fields.

Same for the method args: `since_state: &str`, `since_query_state: &str` in calendar.rs:47, event.rs:60, event.rs:162, event_notification.rs:48, event_notification.rs:153, participant_identity.rs:38. The PLAN.md (lines 113-115, 142, 195, 244, 264) explicitly typed these as `&State` — the implementation diverged from the plan.

Consequence: callers cannot use type-system to prevent mixing up `Id` and `State` strings. Echoing back `response.state` to `since_state` round-trips through `String` losing semantic identity.

Cross-crate note: jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs has identical `String` typing. Same comment about lock state applies.

This is a Section 1 maintainer-burden flag, not a correctness flag — it works today, but the type system is not earning its keep on the most-handled tokens in the API.
notes: Subsumed by JMAP-6by7 (the 0.2.0 typed-Id epic). Migration to State newtype is part of the broader typed-parameter pass across *-client crates. Will be addressed in JMAP-6by7.1 (calendars-client reference impl).
title: state fields are String, jmap-types provides State newtype
